Maintenance proposal, expiry, current preconditions and explicit execute.

Exact work-order identity; accepted workflow does not mean repaired.

Ride SCADA • ticketing • vision • CMMS • ERP/POS • workforce • BMS • water • weather • GIS
CONTEXT / IMPLEMENTED
OpenUSD + native OVStage/OVRTX; quality-aware live view, replay, saved comparisons and static design queries.
ENTERPRISE / PROPOSED
Vendor read adapters, authenticated CMMS writes, qualified roster evidence and approved signage requests.
FOX-inspired architecture; NVIDIA FOX, NemoClaw and OpenShell are not installed. Spatial queries and weather previews remain separate from the uncalibrated forecast.
ASTER PARK  /  CURRENT INCIDENT / ACTUAL GPU APP
INTERIM
An incident can reach a work order directly
Actual Horde L40 app/browser acceptance • verified application release afa84a1
Actual app: frozen source observations
Live asset entry selects the target without a write or forecast
Explicit direct execution creates an order; ride remains closed
Reload retrieves the accepted receipt using GET only
Mobile layout fits the viewport
Saved-comparison workflow still functions
Lost response + reload retries the same request and expiry
4 scripted steps instead of 7 via a saved comparison. This is a UI path comparison, not a measured human productivity gain.
Current status, inspection and open orders are frozen with source evidence. Dispatch accepts a synthetic workflow; it does not repair equipment or reopen a ride.
ASTER PARK  /  DESIGN ALTERNATIVE / NATIVE RTX
INTERIM
Does the dining connection fix access?
Matched native OVStage/OVRTX captures • same camera • separate authored design layer
BASELINE: unreachable in authored graph
DINING DESIGN: 40.852 m route in the graph
Close connector → unreachable
Step-free filter → unreachable; entry threshold unresolved
34.04 s assumes 1.2 m/s; no density or queue delay
Static geometry and a partial authored graph. This is not certified accessibility, physical guest guidance, spare service capacity or forecast validation.
ASTER PARK  /  INDEPENDENT VALUE REVIEW
INTERIM
A useful test can reject the cleverer policy
Independent policy accounting • 324 synthetic cases • 972 outcomes • source d3dca3d
Planner and simple rule choose identical schedules
Different choices: extra staff costs EUR56 per case
Extra staff produces no waiting improvement
Doing nothing strictly dominates the planner choice

Across all cases: +1.701 completed service visits, −28.883 guest-min waiting and +EUR18.667 labor versus the simple rule. Different-choice subgroup: +5.102 visits, −86.648 guest-min and +EUR56. These are grid averages, not expected real outcomes.

Local checkpoint: 407 CPU/application checks passed; three browser modules skipped there. Separate browser environment: 40 checks passed. Actual GPU incident walkthrough: six checks. Scopes and revisions differ; these are not one combined production qualification.
The evaluator omits minimum-coverage constraints, donor depletion/setup loss and replenishment cost. Doing nothing is not advice to understaff. No measured ROI or real park productivity claim.
ASTER PARK  /  NEXT DECISION / RUN STATUS
INTERIM
A narrow pilot can answer the value question
Start with one ride, its maintenance process and one duty-manager workflow.
1 / Establish evidence
Map OEM/CMMS asset IDs, timestamps, inspection states and actual work-order history. Read-only integration first.
2 / Measure the task
Compare alert-to-verified-order time, clicks, incorrect/duplicate orders and operator understanding against today's workflow.
3 / Test decisions
Calibrate arrivals, service, staffing qualifications, delivery delays and cost. Keep do-nothing and simple-rule baselines.
4 / Expand deliberately
Only then add a scoped authenticated CMMS request; validate path geometry before coupling guest movement to forecasts.

still in progress

Two independent tracks:

• read-only GPU observation

Planned window: 19 Oct 19:47 to 20 Oct 03:47 UTC. These are planned times, not completion evidence.
A known deployment interruption remains in the record. Final counts require both completed ledgers.
Next success criterion: a verified operational outcome that an operator values, with measured effort, error rates and clear limits.
